Hi all,

Thanks — attaching a suggested legal paragraph for Exhibit A that aims to balance Acme's predictability needs with Redwood's operational constraints. Primary principles: deterministic lookback windows, one mid-quarter prorated true-up allowed, and an explicit definition of "Compatible Model" for fallback.

Proposed language (suggestion for Exhibit A — Price Collar / Trigger Matrix):
"
1. Definitions. For purposes of this Exhibit, 'Lookback Window' means the preceding 30 calendar days measured at the end of each billing cycle. 'Compatible Model' means a model variant with equivalent token support and comparable architecture family as determined by Redwood's Model Certification matrix.

2. Collar Trigger & Reset. A Price Collar triggers when a customer's 30-day rolling average usage exceeds the Collar Upper threshold defined in the Schedule. If usage remains above the threshold for two consecutive billing cycles (i.e., sustained growth), the contract will migrate the Customer to the higher tier effective the first day of the next billing cycle. Transient spikes that do not persist for two consecutive billing cycles will not trigger a permanent tier migration.

3. Mid-Quarter True-Up. Redwood will perform a prorated mid-quarter true-up if the Customer's usage exceeds the higher tier by more than 20% in any single billing cycle. The prorated charge shall apply from the date of the exceedance through the end of that billing cycle and shall be reconciled at the next invoice. Customers are limited to one (1) mid-quarter prorated true-up per fiscal quarter unless otherwise agreed in writing.

4. Fallback & Downgrade Mechanics. If the preferred hardware class is unavailable, Redwood may route traffic to a Compatible Model. Redwood will provide notice in the Console and apply any applicable temporary uplift as set forth in the Schedule (not to exceed 15% of the standard token rate). Customer may opt to pause non-critical workloads for the duration of the downgrade.

This language preserves predictability while giving Redwood operational flexibility. I can tighten the thresholds if Acme needs more conservative protections.

Attaching: legal-exhibitA-suggestion.docx

Regards,
Monica Patel

- The one mid-quarter true-up is fine, but we need clearer caps for total quarterly exposure (Finance wants a maximum quarterly adjustment equal to 10% of forecasted spend for that quarter).
- Regarding fallback uplift: 15% cap sounds reasonable, but we want a guaranteed SLA floor (P95 inference latency delta not to exceed X ms) or an option to opt into queued capacity rather than an automatic downgrade.

If Redwood can accept 45-day lookback and the quarterly exposure cap language (we can share suggested wording), we can proceed to signature quickly. Are you able to take these edits?

Alice — appreciate the constructive counterproposals. We discussed with Finance and Engineering and propose the following compromise to move to signature: 

Agreed changes:
- Lookback Window: adopt 45 calendar days as Acme requested (deterministic, reduces oscillation).
- Mid-Quarter True-Up: allow one prorated mid-quarter true-up; cap the total quarterly exposure resulting from true-ups at 10% of the original quarterly forecast (as requested).
- Fallback: Redwood will include an option in the Exhibit for Customer to elect (i) automatic downgrade to Compatible Model with a temporary uplift not to exceed 12%, or (ii) queued capacity (best-effort) with no uplift; Redwood will commit to publishing P95 latency delta ranges for the Compatible Models in the Console.

Next steps:

- Jonas will add the Compatible Model latency deltas to the tech appendix.
- I will upload the revised Order Form to DocuSign and share the link for signature once Monica confirms wording.
